<reason>Close, high-quality debate. B won the live clash: easier monthly pause/split/reconfigure is not just anti-cable hygiene; it turns the middle household into a peak-chaser and leaves next year's library underfunded. A's coexistence concession never recovered after B showed that a discount without troughs is a coupon, that addressable is not revenue, and that peaks, no troughs, and no higher sticker cannot travel together.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's demolition of A's 'annual plans can compete beside a one-toggle default': without friction the four-month household never buys twelve, so the motion converts remaining middling payers into tourists rather than keeping a real open trade.</best_rebuttal>
